title: Choose KHOJ's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Call (lost-and-found loudspeaker, in glass and fire). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Call
options.lineage: the mela's khoya-paya loudspeaker booth, rendered in frosted glass and fire
options.thesis: Finding someone feels like calling their name across the crowd: the answer comes back colder or hotter.
options.viewport: Glass status bar; a radar of sound arcs with each person as a name chip, blue when far and burning gold when near; a big SOS dock above a four-tab bar.
options.risk: The loudspeaker idea could read as mela-only; it lives in the motion of the arcs, never as a literal horn.

raised.raise: Member rows become strict ruled modules with a small coloured tab, nothing wasted.
The radar header names the span in view: nearest and farthest person, like guide words.
One element owns each screen: the radar on Home, the heat field on Find, the button on SOS.
Alarms invert the whole frame for one beat, so an emergency is impossible to miss.

options.label: Diya Night
options.thesis: Every person in your group is a diya in the dark: the closer they are, the bigger and brighter the flame.
options.viewport: A night field with your diya at the centre and family flames around it at true bearing; a sparkler burst when someone is found.
options.risk: Dark ground with glowing accents is the look most apps in this lane land on, and it is festival-specific.

options.label: Station Board
options.lineage: Indian Railways departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Your group as a live departure board: people ranked by distance, and a changed status stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: A ranked board of members (name, distance, direction, last heard) with the SOS pass stub pinned below.
options.case: Fuses well: everyone knows a station board, and ranking by distance plus held alerts is clear; loses on the finding moment's wow.
options.risk: Can read as a utility timetable with little delight.

options.label: Course Line
options.lineage: orienteering maps and their purple course
options.thesis: One reserved purple line from you to the person you seek; everything else is quiet ground.
options.viewport: A white field with contour-like distance rings, your position, and a purple leg to the target with control circles for meeting point and last seen.
options.case: Fuses on clarity (one colour for the active leg); loses on identification, since few users know orienteering.
options.risk: Looks like a map app without a map, which we deliberately do not download.

options.label: Dense Modules
options.thesis: Pack every status into ruled modules with red tabs.
options.viewport: A mosaic of small boxed modules.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a stressed person in a crowd cannot read tiny dense type.
options.kept: Strict ruled-module discipline for member rows.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Black text in a fixed measure with guide words naming the span in view.
options.viewport: A typeset column with guide words at the head.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reading a page is the opposite of a glance in a crowd.
options.kept: Guide words: the header names nearest and farthest person in view.

options.label: Guide-Map Lobes
options.thesis: Each screen is one swelling lobe of flat colour.
options.viewport: One green lobe owning the screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful but implies a map of the venue we do not have.
options.risk: Suggests venue maps KHOJ does not ship.

options.label: Data Strobe
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields that strobe.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing is unsafe and cold for frightened families.
options.kept: Full-frame inversion reserved as the alarm signal.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Material 3 family locator, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top app bar, a list of member cards with distance and direction, an SOS FAB.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other locator apps by design.
